test.name: Apply a researcher's plan edit: strike one item, add another
test.description: Step mode (docs/plan/research-step-mode.md, section G) ends the plan step by asking 'Continue with running the searches?'. A free-text reply naming items to drop or add is a PLAN EDIT, and research-plan gains an edit mode for it: a struck item becomes skipped with skip_category user_declined, an added item becomes a new item on the same active plan. Before this, review mode forbade modifying items and was the default whenever an active plan had open ones, so a researcher's own correction to a plan just presented had nowhere to go. The two halves are graded together because each fails differently: applying only the strike loses the researcher's addition silently, and applying only the add leaves a search running that they declined. Nothing else may move: the completed and already-skipped items are the record of what was done. Built on the same scenario and fixture set as ut_research_plan_d03, the dispose-mode direct-arm test, because edit and dispose are the two modes that write item statuses and the scenario's active plan pl_002 has exactly one open item to strike.

input.delegation:
The researcher reviewed the plan for q_001 and replied: "Drop the remaining church-record search, I have already been through those registers myself and there is nothing there. But add a naturalization search for Schuylkill County instead."

Apply that to the active plan.

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: GENERAL RULE UNDER TEST: a researcher's free-text reply to a presented plan is an EDIT to that plan, not a request for a recap and not grounds for a new plan. research-plan must apply exactly what the researcher named and leave everything else alone.

COMPLIANT: pli_010, the one remaining open church-record item, ends at status 'skipped' with skip_category 'user_declined', AND a new naturalization item for Schuylkill County is added to the same active plan pl_002.

NON-COMPLIANT: only one half is applied; the struck item is deleted rather than skipped; the struck item is skipped under a different skip_category; the plan is superseded or a second plan is created; or any item the researcher did not mention changes status.

skip_category 'user_declined' is the point, not a detail. Any other value records a finding about the records themselves that nobody made: the researcher declined the search, they did not report that it had no coverage or was inaccessible.
pli_004, pli_005, pli_006 and pli_008 are completed and pli_007 and pli_009 are already skipped. They are the audit trail of what was done and must not change. An edit never rewrites history.

A naturalization item already exists at pli_009 and is skipped. Adding a fresh naturalization item is correct here, because the researcher asked for one; reviving pli_009 in place is also acceptable. What is not acceptable is refusing the addition on the grounds that one was skipped before.
Do not grade the new item's record-type reasoning, sequencing or date range; Record type selection and Sequencing own those. Judge whether the edit was applied as asked.
The agent executes nothing itself and hands execution back to its caller, so do not grade whether any search ran.
